bdb3bb0a662a: Create Multiple Salesforce Tasks at Once, From a Calendar
d0148a930073: Create Salesforce Tasks From a Calendar: Pick the Days, Save Once
c0e8a4845957: Create multiple Salesforce Tasks at once: pick the days on a calendar, set the subject, status and priority, and save one Task per day. No Flow, no Apex.
fa7f63491473: How do I create multiple tasks at once in Salesforce?
d100981db807: Put the MultiDatePick Dates component on the record page with Task as the object it saves. Click every day that needs a task, type the subject, and click Save. MultiDatePick creates one standard Salesforce Task per day, each with its own due date and linked to the record, in a single save. No Flow and no Apex are involved.
06bfc2ca6e8a: Can I create Salesforce tasks on dates that do not follow a pattern?
7e24d1f9e19c: Yes. You click the exact days you need, such as the 3rd, the 11th and the 24th, and each one becomes a task. When the days do follow a pattern, the Add Recurring Pattern button fills them in for you: every Tuesday, every other week, or the 1st or last weekday of each month.
5b6a24982904: Which record pages can create tasks this way?
34e0fb1e6117: Any record that tasks can be related to. Accounts, Opportunities, Cases and custom objects with activities link through Related To (WhatId). Contacts and Leads link through Name (WhoId). On a Contact page, Salesforce also fills in the contact's account, so the new tasks show on the account too.
eac66249a4de: Can every new task get the same priority, status or assignee?
8d2b00f7e358: Yes. The status picker sets the Status of the tasks being saved. Default Field Values fills any other field on every new task, for example Priority=High, a Comments line, or OwnerId set to a user's Id to assign the tasks to that person. Without it, tasks are assigned to the person who saves them, as usual in Salesforce.
2fe02d109313: Can I see my Salesforce tasks on a calendar?
549c4b13fbcf: Yes. On a record page the calendar shows that record's tasks in their status colors. On an app or Home page, turn on Show All Records and set Record Filter to OwnerId=ME for a calendar of your own tasks, with each subject written in its day. Hover a day for the details, or add the Agenda view for a list of them.

57fc801df76c: When the days follow a pattern

Each day still saves as its own Task, so you can move or skip one without touching the rest.

591a54b3f115: Set it up in the Setup Wizard
27b7ff293814: No code, and no Flow to build. The Setup Wizard writes the configuration and the component reads it:
699595bc565a: <t1>Choose where the calendar goes.</t1> Open the MultiDatePick Setup Wizard tab, pick the record page (Account here) and the one record per date shape.
fd3905f93940: <t1>Save each pick as a Task.</t1> On the Fields screen click <t2>Task</t2>, then check the link to the page: <t3>Related To ID (WhatId)</t3> on an Account, or <t4>Name ID (WhoId)</t4> on a Contact or Lead. The wizard fills in <t5>Due Date Only (ActivityDate)</t5> and <t6>Subject</t6>.
d8d4cf195fd6: <t1>Fill in the rest.</t1> Type a default subject, untick Append Date/Time to Record Name to keep subjects clean, and enter Default Field Values such as <t2>Priority=High</t2>. Save the config under a name like <t3>Account_Tasks</t3>.
d88803f6df97: <t1>Drop the component on the page.</t1> In Lightning App Builder, add the MultiDatePick Dates component to the Account page and enter the name in <t2>Config Name</t2>.
aa602a784073: Task in one click: Related To, Due Date Only and Subject, plus a default subject and Priority=High.
3f4cfd86ed64: Status colors come from your Task Status values, so Completed can be green and Deferred grey. Change the config later and every page that uses it picks the change up on its next load.
